reason: Attacked at the manuscript and it holds to the letter. I did not take the verifier's word for the transcript but fetched the Massachusetts Historical Society page it cites and read the passage in context. It prints: I long to hear that you have declared an independency -- and by the way in the new Code of Laws which I suppose it will be necessary for you to make I desire you would Remember the Ladies, and be more generous and favourable to them than your ancestors. followed by Do not put such unlimited power into the hands of the Husbands. So every element of the proposal is confirmed: the British spelling favourable rather than favorable, which a modernising text would have flattened; the comma after ancestors' clause; Abigail's own capitals on Remember the Ladies; and, most importantly, that the full stop after ancestors is the manuscript's own, so the quotation is not cut mid-sentence and closed with punctuation no edition prints, which is the failure that had to be corrected in the July Jane Eyre carry-in. The quotation does begin inside a longer sentence, at I desire, but it begins at a clean clause boundary and the first word is already a capital I, so nothing has been raised or altered; that is the same lift the month already accepts in the Addams and Sewell carry-ins. Locator: the MHS page confirms the letter is a multi-day composition of 31 March to 5 April 1776, exactly as the source says, and the Remember the Ladies passage stands in the opening portion written on 31 March, headed Braintree, so the dateline, the span and the within-letter placement are all right. Attribution: genuinely hers and not a misattribution-list trap; this is one of the few famous lines of the period that is exactly what it is said to be, and the source names the archive and the edition rather than a quotation site. Scope: a private family letter of 1776, so it is Correspondence and not the oratory the Makers own, nothing post-1999, nothing needing a warning, and it is a brisk and good-humoured demand rather than anything bleak at six in the morning. Theme: the month is what is owed, and this is the founding American sentence about a debt that was not paid. Tag Correspondence is the form of the work. Form: the source leads with her name, carries no dash and no straight double quote, and the quotation ends in a full stop. shipped.js: not shipped, no near opening, not banned, abigail adams at 2 of 3 from months 3 and 7. TWO CAUTIONS, neither a refutation. First, the source line is 136 characters against the 140 cap, so it has four characters of headroom and any addition to it will break the rule; if the editor wants to add a page or a volume, something else has to come out. Second, this is Abigail Adams's THIRD and last line of the year, which is the right way to spend it, but it does close her out.
